# SK2041 — `base.Equals` or `base.GetHashCode` resolves to `object`'s

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

An equality member calls `base.Equals` or `base.GetHashCode` where the base is `System.Object`, so the delegation it was written to perform returns reference identity and the identity hash.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Correctness |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 1.3 |

## Why

The override exists to replace identity with value semantics, and `base` is identity — the one thing it was written to stop doing. `base.GetHashCode()` inside `GetHashCode` returns the runtime's per-instance number, so two equal objects hash differently and the type is unusable as a dictionary key however carefully `Equals` was written. `base.Equals(other)` inside `Equals` returns reference equality, so the override answers the question it was overriding. It is a copy-paste result and a generated-stub result, and it reads as diligence.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
sealed class Key {
    public string Name { get; init; } = "";

    public override bool Equals(object? other) => base.Equals(other);

    public override int GetHashCode() => base.GetHashCode();
}
```

Write:

```csharp
sealed class Key {
    public string Name { get; init; } = "";

    public override bool Equals(object? other) => other is Key key && key.Name == Name;

    public override int GetHashCode() => Name.GetHashCode();
}
```

## When it does not fire

The receiver must be spelled `base`, the call must sit inside an equality member of the declaring type — `Equals`, `GetHashCode` or `CompareTo` — and the call must **bind** to a member of `System.Object`. An intermediate base class that overrides equality is doing real work, and delegating to it is correct and is never reported. `base.GetHashCode()` in a struct binds to `ValueType.GetHashCode`, which does hash the fields, and is likewise not reported. ⚠ **Fixless, and the reason is that both repairs are edits somebody has to choose between.** Deleting the call changes what the member returns, and replacing it needs to know which fields identity is made of — the one thing the analysis cannot recover from a body that never mentions them. A generated `HashCode.Combine(...)` over every field would be a guess presented as a repair, which is worse than no fix in exactly the situation where the author was already not paying attention.

## Configuration

- `dotnet_diagnostic.SK2041.severity`
